topic: Applicant claim dialog and wallet receipt integration
behavior: The dialog submits one no-options claim request per application/organization/holder scope while pending; close/reopen shares the request, wallet choice only changes transport.

The Rust endpoint controls pending offer reuse and expiry renewal. Unsupported holder destination and Canvas mirror controls are removed from this dialog; there is no claim that those options are implemented.
Late catalogues, offers, errors, status reads and wallet-open results from an old application, organization, wallet or view are discarded.
Refresh hides old actionable QR content while pending and after failure. Retrying requires an explicit user action.

Read-only holder application status polls every two seconds while visible and nonterminal, coalesces return events, and never POSTs issuance. Confirmed CLAIMED, EXPIRED and BLOCKED projections replace active QR content.
Application and organization identity must match on readback. Failed or mismatched readback clears the actionable invite.
Claim POST and raw application GET use the same offer normalization, retaining offer URI, expiration and Rust status/capabilities.
Mobile and actual desktop child use one shared wallet opener. An asynchronous launch becomes invalid after close, scope change, wallet change, offer change or confirmed receipt.
Email opens a mailto draft and does not claim email delivery. The UI does not promise a fresh offer for every opening.

verification.phase: Original existing dialog tests at unchanged base
verification.boundary: Existing MUI focus-restoration teardown failures. Final test fixture opens from a real focused button; no production FocusTrap or test framework configuration was weakened.

verification.phase: 13-case contract regression input against unchanged base
verification.boundary: These 13 cases predate the six final read-only status/normalization/handoff integration cases. This is not a claim that all 19 final cases were run before the change.

verification.phase: Final parent and real invite/QR child
verification.boundary: The third pattern was an absent path and selected no tests. The log records two actual files, 31 cases. Canvas ApplicationForm is independently verified by the unchanged 15-case canvas-claim-return record, not counted as executed in this command. Child tests render the real invite and QR components; parent tests mock the child and controlled service responses.
Production TypeScript only. No new full application build or broad test-source TypeScript pass is claimed.

finalParentNamedCases: acquires one server-governed offer and loads organization-scoped wallet links
does not offer Canvas consent or destination selection that the Rust claim path cannot execute
explains when the issuer has not activated an OID4VCI issuance flow
changes browser wallet transport without starting another issuance
waits for a delayed wallet catalogue and applies the preference without duplicate claims
ignores the previous application response after switching applications
does not let a late organization registry replace the current wallet catalogue
shares a pending claim across close and reopen and restores focus to the opener
hides the previous invite while a refresh is pending and never restores it after failure
uses the selected Spruce wallet-specific URI for the mobile handoff
does not navigate when a delayed wallet link resolves after the dialog closes
uses the Rust expired claim state and offers a server retry
replaces the invite with confirmed receipt through read-only polling
retains the raw Rust offer URL and expiration when the application is refreshed
invalidates a pending mobile wallet handoff when readback confirms the credential was claimed
coalesces browser return reads and keeps blocked claims from displaying an active QR
discards a late return read after switching applications and removes its listeners on unmount
does not preserve an actionable invite after failed or mismatched status readback
describes mailto as an email draft without claiming the message was sent
boundaries: Controlled service responses and jsdom browser surfaces do not prove a deployed Rust/wallet round trip, native application launch, credential storage or released master.

The actual native claim API and concurrency behavior have separate Rust HTTP/service regressions. The actual desktop invitation child has a separate 12-case record; those 12 executions overlap the final 31-case run and are not additive unique cases.
Canvas ApplicationForm return behavior is verified separately with 15 cases at c971c40. No test requires treating browser return or closing as receipt.

Earlier exploratory claim-dialog-first-fix/claim-dialog-regression logs modeled request options before the unsupported Rust contract was identified. They are superseded exploratory results and are not retained or cited as final production verification.
Automatic server retirement and fresh production video/audio qualification remain unperformed.
